verses.text: These are the words of Nehemiah son of Hacaliah. In the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, I was at the palace in Susa.
One of my brothers, Hanani, came with some men from Judah. I asked them about the Jews who had survived the exile and about Jerusalem.
They told me, "The survivors of the exile there in the province are in serious trouble and facing disgrace. Jerusalem's wall is broken down, and its gates have been burned."
When I heard that, I sat down and wept. For several days I mourned, fasted, and prayed before the God of heaven.
I said, "LORD, God of heaven, great and awesome God, you keep your covenant and show faithful love to those who love you and keep your commands.

Please open your eyes and listen closely to the prayer I bring before you day and night for your servants, the people of Israel. I confess the sins we Israelites have committed against you. My own family and I have sinned too.
We've acted wickedly toward you and failed to keep the commands, statutes, and rulings you gave your servant Moses.
Please remember what you told your servant Moses: 'If you are unfaithful, I'll scatter you among the nations.
But if you return to me and keep my commands, even if you've been driven to the farthest reaches under heaven, I'll gather you from there and bring you to the place I've chosen for my name to dwell.'
These are your servants and your people, whom you rescued by your great power and your strong hand.
Lord, please listen to my prayer and to the prayers of your servants who delight in honoring your name. Give me success today and let this man show me mercy." I was the king's cupbearer at the time.
In the month of Nisan, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, I picked up the wine that had been set out and handed it to the king. I'd never looked sad in front of him before.
The king asked me, "Why do you look so sad? You're clearly not sick. You must be carrying sorrow in your heart." I was terrified.
I said, "May the king live forever! How could I keep from looking sad when the city where my ancestors are buried lies in ruins and its gates have burned down?"
The king asked, "What do you want?" I prayed to the God of heaven.
Then I said, "If it pleases the king and your servant has found favor with you, please send me to Judah, to the city where my ancestors are buried, so I can rebuild it."
With the queen sitting beside him, the king asked, "How long will your trip take, and when will you be back?" The king agreed to send me, and I gave him a date.
I also asked, "If it pleases the king, give me letters to the governors of the province Beyond the River so they'll let me pass through safely on my way to Judah.

Please also give me a letter to Asaph, who manages the king's forest, asking him to supply timber for the gates of the fortress near the temple, for the city wall, and for the house where I'll live." The king granted what I asked because the good hand of my God was on me.
When I reached the governors of the province Beyond the River, I gave them the king's letters. The king had sent army officers and horsemen with me.
When Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official heard about it, they were deeply upset that someone had come to help the Israelites.
I arrived in Jerusalem and stayed there for three days.
Then I went out at night with a few men. I hadn't told anyone what my God had put in my heart to do for Jerusalem. The only animal we took was the one I rode.
I went out by the Valley Gate that night, toward the Jackal's Well and the Dung Gate. I inspected Jerusalem's walls, which lay broken down, and its gates, which had been burned.
Then I went on to the Spring Gate and the King's Pool, but my mount couldn't get through there.
So I went up the ravine that night and inspected the wall. Then I turned back and returned through the Valley Gate.
The officials had no idea where I had gone or what I was doing. I still hadn't told the Jews, the priests, the nobles, the officials, or anyone else who would do the work.
Then I told them, "You see the trouble we're in. Jerusalem lies in ruins, and its gates have been burned. Come on, let's rebuild Jerusalem's wall so we won't live in disgrace anymore."
I told them how God's good hand had been on me and what the king had said to me. They answered, "Let's get up and build." Then they got ready to do the good work.
When Sanballat the Horonite, Tobiah the Ammonite official, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they mocked and looked down on us. They said, "What are you doing? Are you rebelling against the king?"
I replied, "The God of heaven will give us success. We're his servants, and we're going to rebuild. You have no share, no claim, and no historic right in Jerusalem."

Eliashib the high priest and his fellow priests got to work and rebuilt the Sheep Gate. They set it apart as holy and hung its doors. They consecrated the wall as far as the Tower of Hammeah and the Tower of Hananel.
The men of Jericho built next to them, and Zaccur son of Imri built next to the men of Jericho.
The sons of Hassenaah rebuilt the Fish Gate. They set the beams in place and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.
Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, made repairs next to them. Beside him worked Meshullam son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel, and beside Meshullam worked Zadok son of Baana.
The people of Tekoa worked on the next section, though their nobles refused to put their shoulders to the Lord's work.
Joiada son of Paseah and Meshullam son of Besodeiah repaired the Old Gate. They set the beams in place and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.
Next to them, Melatiah from Gibeon and Jadon from Meronoth worked with the men of Gibeon and Mizpah on the residence of the governor of the province Beyond the River.
Uzziel son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, worked on the next section. Hananiah, one of the perfumers, worked beside him. They strengthened Jerusalem as far as the Broad Wall.
Next to them, Rephaiah son of Hur, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, made repairs.
Jedaiah son of Harumaph worked next on the section across from his own house, with Hattush son of Hashabneiah working beside him.
Malchijah son of Harim and Hasshub son of Pahathmoab repaired another section, including the Tower of the Furnaces.
Next to them, Shallum son of Hallohesh, ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, worked with his daughters.
Hanun and the people of Zanoah rebuilt the Valley Gate. They set up its doors, bolts, and bars and repaired a thousand cubits of wall as far as the Dung Gate.
Malchijah son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth Haccherem, rebuilt the Dung Gate and installed its doors, bolts, and bars.

Shallun son of Colhozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, rebuilt and roofed the Spring Gate and fitted its doors, bolts, and bars. He repaired the wall by the Pool of Shelah near the king's garden as far as the steps going down from the City of David.
Next came Nehemiah son of Azbuk, ruler of half the district of Beth Zur. He repaired the section reaching the place opposite David's tombs, the man-made pool, and the House of the Warriors.
After him the Levites made repairs under Rehum son of Bani. Next to him, Hashabiah, ruler of half the district of Keilah, made repairs for his district.
Next their fellow Levites made repairs under Bavvai son of Henadad, ruler of half the district of Keilah.
Beside him, Ezer son of Jeshua, ruler of Mizpah, repaired another section across from the path up to the armory at the bend in the wall.
After him, Baruch son of Zabbai worked hard on another section, from the bend in the wall to the door of the high priest Eliashib's house.
Next, Meremoth son of Uriah, son of Hakkoz, repaired the section from the door of Eliashib's house to the far end of the house.
The priests from the surrounding area worked on the next section.
Next, Benjamin and Hasshub repaired the section across from their house. Azariah son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah, worked on the section beside his own house.
After him, Binnui son of Henadad repaired the section from Azariah's house to the bend and the corner of the wall.
Palal son of Uzai worked opposite the bend and the tower that juts out from the upper royal palace near the guard courtyard. Pedaiah son of Parosh worked beside him.
The temple servants lived on Ophel, as far as the place across from the Water Gate on the east and the tower that juts out.
Next the people of Tekoa repaired another section, from opposite the large projecting tower to the wall of Ophel.
Above the Horse Gate, the priests made repairs, each across from his own house.
Next, Zadok son of Immer made repairs across from his own house. Shemaiah son of Shecaniah, the guard at the East Gate, worked beside him.
Hananiah son of Shelemiah and Hanun, Zalaph's sixth son, repaired the next section. Meshullam son of Berechiah then made repairs across from his room.
After him, Malchijah the goldsmith repaired as far as the house used by the temple servants and merchants, opposite the Hammiphkad Gate, and up to the passage at the corner.
Between the passage at the corner and the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants made repairs.
When Sanballat heard that we were rebuilding the wall, he was furious and began mocking the Jews.

In front of his associates and the army of Samaria, he said, "What are these weak Jews doing? Do they think they can fortify the city? Will they offer sacrifices? Will they finish in a day? Can they bring burned stones back to life out of those piles of rubble?"
Tobiah the Ammonite was beside him. He said, "Even a fox climbing on that stone wall would knock it down."
Hear us, our God, because they despise us. Turn their insults back on them. Let them be plundered in a land where they're taken captive.
Don't cover their guilt or erase their sin from before you, because they've insulted the builders.
We kept building until the entire wall was joined up to half its height. The people were determined to work.
When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, the Ammonites, and the people of Ashdod heard that the repairs to Jerusalem's walls were moving ahead and the gaps were closing, they became furious.
They plotted together to attack Jerusalem and throw us into confusion.
We prayed to our God and posted guards day and night because of the threat.
Meanwhile, the people of Judah said, "The workers who carry the loads are wearing out. There's so much rubble that we can't rebuild the wall."
Our enemies said, "They won't know or see a thing until we're among them. Then we'll kill them and stop the work."
The Jews who lived near them came to warn us again and again from all directions: "Wherever you turn, they'll attack us."
So I stationed people in family groups at the lowest, most exposed places behind the wall, with their swords, spears, and bows.

After looking things over, I stood up and told the nobles, officials, and everyone else, "Don't be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome. Fight for your brothers, your sons and daughters, your wives, and your homes."
When our enemies heard that we knew about their plan and that God had frustrated it, we all went back to the wall, each to our work.
From then on, half my servants worked and half held spears, shields, bows, and armor. The officials stood behind all the people of Judah.
The builders and the people carrying supplies took up their loads, working with one hand and holding a weapon with the other.
Each builder wore a sword at his side while he worked, and the trumpeter stayed with me.
I told the nobles, officials, and everyone else, "This is a large job spread over a wide area, and we're working far apart along the wall.
When you hear the trumpet, gather where it sounds. Our God will fight for us."
We kept working, with half the men holding spears from dawn until the stars came out.
I also told the people, "Have each man and his servant spend the night in Jerusalem, so they can guard us at night and work during the day."
None of us took off our clothes, whether my brothers, my servants, the guards with me, or I. We took our weapons even when we went for water.
Then the people and their wives raised a loud outcry against their fellow Jews.
Some said, "There are a lot of us, with all our sons and daughters. We need grain to eat so we can stay alive."
Others said, "We're mortgaging our fields, vineyards, and houses to get grain during the famine."
Still others said, "We've borrowed money to pay the king's tax and put up our fields and vineyards as collateral.

We're the same flesh and blood as our fellow Jews, and our children are just like theirs. Yet we're having to give our sons and daughters into slavery, and some of our daughters are already enslaved. We can't do anything about it because other people own our fields and vineyards now."
I was furious when I heard their outcry and what they were saying.
After thinking it over, I confronted the nobles and officials. I said, "You're charging interest to your own people." Then I called a large assembly to deal with them.

I told them, "As far as we could, we've bought back our fellow Jews who had been sold to other nations. Now you're selling your own people, so we have to buy them back again?" They kept quiet. They had no answer.
I went on, "What you're doing is wrong. You should live with reverence for our God, so the nations that oppose us have no reason to mock us.
My brothers, my servants, and I are also lending them money and grain. Let's stop charging interest.
Give back their fields, vineyards, olive groves, and houses today. Return the hundredth part you've been charging them in money, grain, new wine, and oil."
They said, "We'll give it back and demand nothing from them. We'll do what you've said." I called the priests and made the lenders swear in front of them to keep their promise.

I shook out the fold of my robe and said, "May God shake out anyone who breaks this promise from their house and from the fruit of their work. May they be shaken out and left empty like this." The whole assembly said, "Amen," and praised the LORD. The people kept their promise.

From the time I was appointed governor of Judah, in the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, to his thirty-second year, a total of twelve years, neither I nor my brothers took the governor's food allowance.

The governors before me burdened the people by taking bread and wine from them, along with forty shekels of silver. Even their servants ruled over the people. I lived differently out of reverence for God.
I kept working on the wall. We bought no land, and all my servants were gathered there for the work.
A hundred fifty Jews and officials ate at my table, along with visitors from the surrounding nations.

Every day one ox, six choice sheep, and some poultry were prepared for me. Every ten days there was a fresh supply of all kinds of wine. Even with all this, I never demanded the governor's allowance because the people were already carrying a heavy burden.
My God, remember me for good for everything I've done for these people.
Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I'd rebuilt the wall and closed all the gaps, though I still hadn't hung the doors in the gates.
Sanballat and Geshem sent me a message: "Come meet us in one of the villages in the plain of Ono." They were planning to harm me.
I sent messengers back: "I'm doing important work and can't come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to meet with you?"
They sent me the same invitation four times, and each time I gave them the same answer.
The fifth time Sanballat sent his servant to me with an unsealed letter.
It said, "The nations are saying, and Gashmu confirms it, that you and the Jews are planning a rebellion. That's why you're rebuilding the wall. They say you plan to become their king.
They also say you've appointed prophets to announce in Jerusalem, 'There's a king in Judah!' These reports will reach the king. Come and let's talk this over."
I sent back this reply: "None of what you're saying is happening. You've made it all up yourself."
They were all trying to frighten us, thinking, "They'll lose heart and give up, and the work will never be finished." But now, God, strengthen my hands.

I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, son of Mehetabel, who was shut in at home. He said, "Let's meet inside the temple in God's house and shut the doors. They're coming to kill you. They'll come for you tonight."
I replied, "Should someone in my position run away? Who in my position could enter the temple to save his life? I won't go in."
I realized God hadn't sent him. Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him to deliver this prophecy against me.
They hired him to frighten me into doing what he said and committing a sin. Then they could spread a bad report about me and disgrace me.
Remember, my God, what Tobiah and Sanballat have done. Remember Noadiah the prophet and the other prophets who tried to frighten me.
So the wall was finished on the twenty-fifth day of Elul, after fifty-two days of work.
When our enemies heard, the nations around us grew afraid and lost their confidence. They realized our God had done this work.
In those days the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and he wrote back to them.
Many people in Judah had sworn loyalty to him because he was the son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and because his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
They spoke well of what Tobiah had done in front of me and reported my words to him. Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.
Once the wall was rebuilt and I'd hung the doors, the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites were appointed.
I put my brother Hanani and Hananiah, the fortress commander, in charge of Jerusalem. Hananiah was a faithful man who revered God more than most.

I told them, "Keep Jerusalem's gates closed until the sun is hot. While the guards are still on duty, have the doors shut and bar them. Assign people from Jerusalem to guard duty, each at a post near his own house."
The city was large and spread out, yet few people lived there, and the houses had yet to be rebuilt.
God put it in my heart to gather the nobles, officials, and people and register them by family. I found the register of those who had come up first, and here is what it said.
These are the people of the province who returned from exile. King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon had taken them captive. They returned to Jerusalem and Judah, each to their own town.
They came with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah. Here is the count of the Israelite men.
Parosh's descendants numbered two thousand one hundred seventy-two.
Shephatiah's descendants numbered three hundred seventy-two.
Arah's descendants numbered six hundred fifty-two.
Pahathmoab's descendants from the families of Jeshua and Joab numbered two thousand eight hundred eighteen.
Elam's descendants numbered one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
Zattu's descendants numbered eight hundred forty-five.
Zaccai's descendants numbered seven hundred sixty.
Binnui's descendants numbered six hundred forty-eight.
Bebai's descendants numbered six hundred twenty-eight.
Azgad's descendants numbered two thousand three hundred twenty-two.
Adonikam's descendants numbered six hundred sixty-seven.
Bigvai's descendants numbered two thousand sixty-seven.
Adin's descendants numbered six hundred fifty-five.
Ater's descendants through Hezekiah numbered ninety-eight.
Hashum's descendants numbered three hundred twenty-eight.
Bezai's descendants numbered three hundred twenty-four.
Hariph's descendants numbered one hundred twelve.
From Gibeon came ninety-five.
From Bethlehem and Netophah came one hundred eighty-eight.
From Anathoth came one hundred twenty-eight.
From Beth Azmaveth came forty-two.
From Kiriath Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth came seven hundred forty-three.
From Ramah and Geba came six hundred twenty-one.
From Michmas came one hundred twenty-two.
From Bethel and Ai came one hundred twenty-three.
From the other Nebo came fifty-two.
the other Elam's descendants numbered one thousand two hundred fifty-four.
Harim's descendants numbered three hundred twenty.
From Jericho came three hundred forty-five.
From Lod, Hadid, and Ono came seven hundred twenty-one.
Senaah's descendants numbered three thousand nine hundred thirty.
The priests included nine hundred seventy-three descendants of Jedaiah from the family of Jeshua.
Immer's descendants numbered one thousand fifty-two.
Pashhur's descendants numbered one thousand two hundred forty-seven.
Harim's descendants numbered one thousand seventeen.
The Levites included seventy-four descendants of Jeshua and Kadmiel from the family of Hodevah.
The singers were Asaph's descendants, a hundred forty-eight in all.
The gatekeepers came from the families of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai, a hundred thirty-eight in all.
The temple servants came from the families of Ziha, Hasupha, and Tabbaoth,
Keros, Sia, Padon,
Lebana, Hagaba, Salmai,
Hanan, Giddel, Gahar,
Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda,
Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah,
Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim,
Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,
Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha,
Barkos, Sisera, Temah,
Neziah and Hatipha.
The descendants of Solomon's servants came from the families of Sotai, Sophereth, and Perida,
Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,
Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Amon.
The temple servants and the descendants of Solomon's servants numbered three hundred ninety-two altogether.
Some people returned from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer without records to establish their ancestry or show whether they belonged to Israel.
They included the descendants of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda, six hundred forty-two in all.
The priestly families included the descendants of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai. Barzillai had married a daughter of Barzillai the Gileadite and taken the family's name.
They searched for their names in the family records but couldn't find them, so they were disqualified from serving as priests.
The governor told them to refrain from eating the most sacred food until a priest could serve with the Urim and Thummim.
The whole assembly numbered forty-two thousand three hundred sixty,
plus seven thousand three hundred thirty-seven male and female servants. They also had two hundred forty-five men and women who sang.
They had seven hundred thirty-six horses and two hundred forty-five mules,
as well as four hundred thirty-five camels and six thousand seven hundred twenty donkeys.
Some family heads contributed to the work. The governor gave the treasury a thousand darics of gold, fifty basins, and five hundred thirty priestly garments.
Some family heads gave the building fund twenty thousand darics of gold and two thousand two hundred minas of silver.
The rest of the people gave twenty thousand darics of gold, two thousand minas of silver, and sixty-seven priestly garments.
The priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, some of the people, temple servants, and all the Israelites settled in their own towns. By the seventh month the Israelites were in their towns.
All the people gathered together in the square in front of the Water Gate. They asked Ezra the scribe to bring out the Book of the Law of Moses, which the LORD had commanded Israel to follow.
On the first day of the seventh month, Ezra the priest brought the law before the assembly of men, women, and everyone old enough to understand what they heard.
In the square in front of the Water Gate, he read from early morning until noon before the men, women, and everyone who could understand. All the people listened closely to the Book of the Law.

Ezra the scribe stood on a wooden platform built for the occasion. To his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah. To his left stood Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbaddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam.
Ezra opened the book where everyone could see him, because he was standing above the crowd. As he opened it, everyone stood up.
Ezra blessed the LORD, the great God, and all the people lifted their hands and answered, "Amen! Amen!" Then they bowed down and worshiped the LORD with their faces to the ground.
Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the other Levites explained the law while the people stayed in their places.
They read clearly from the Book of God's Law and explained its meaning so the people could understand what they heard.

Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites teaching the people said, "Today is holy to the LORD your God. Don't mourn or weep." The people had all been weeping when they heard the words of the law.
Nehemiah told them, "Go and enjoy rich food and sweet drinks, and send some to anyone who has nothing prepared. Today is holy to our Lord. Don't grieve, because the joy of the LORD is your strength."
The Levites calmed the people, saying, "Be still. This day is holy. Don't grieve."
Then everyone went to eat, drink, share portions of their food, and celebrate, because they'd understood the words read to them.
On the second day the family heads of all the people, along with the priests and Levites, gathered with Ezra the scribe to study the words of the law.
They found that the LORD had commanded through Moses that the Israelites should live in temporary shelters during the festival in the seventh month.

They were to announce this throughout their towns and in Jerusalem: "Go into the hills and bring back branches of olive, wild olive, myrtle, palm, and other leafy trees to build temporary shelters, as written."
The people went out and brought back branches. They made shelters on their roofs and in their courtyards, in the courtyards of God's house, and in the squares at the Water Gate and the Ephraim Gate.
Everyone who had returned from exile built temporary shelters and lived in them. The Israelites hadn't done this in that way since the days of Joshua son of Nun. There was great joy.
Every day, from the first to the last, Ezra read from the Book of God's Law. They celebrated the festival for seven days, and on the eighth day they held a solemn assembly as prescribed.
On the twenty-fourth day of that month, the Israelites assembled to fast. They wore sackcloth and put dirt on themselves.
The descendants of Israel separated themselves from the foreigners and stood to confess their sins and the wrongdoing of their ancestors.
They stood where they were and read from the Book of the Law of the LORD their God for a quarter of the day. For another quarter they confessed their sins and worshiped the LORD their God.
Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the Levites' steps and cried out loudly to the LORD their God.

The Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said, "Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting. May your glorious name be blessed. It is higher than all blessing and praise.

You alone are the LORD. You made heaven, the highest heavens and all their host, the earth and everything on it, and the seas and everything in them. You keep them all alive, and the host of heaven worships you.
You are the LORD God who chose Abram, brought him out of Ur of the Chaldeans, and named him Abraham.

You found him faithful to you and promised by covenant to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites. You kept your promise because you are righteous.
You saw our ancestors suffering in Egypt and heard their cry at the Red Sea.

You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, his officials, and all the people of his land because you knew how arrogantly they'd treated our ancestors. You made a name for yourself that endures to this day.
You split the sea in front of them so they could cross through it on dry ground. You threw their pursuers into the depths like a stone into raging water.
You led them with a pillar of cloud by day and with a pillar of fire at night to light the way they should go.
You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke to them from heaven. You gave them just rulings, true laws, and good statutes and commands.
You made your holy Sabbath known to them and gave them commands, statutes, and law through Moses your servant.
When they were hungry, you gave them bread from heaven. When they were thirsty, you brought them water from a rock. You told them to go in and take possession of the land you'd sworn to give them.
But our ancestors grew proud and stubborn and ignored your commands.

They refused to obey and forgot the wonders you'd done among them. They grew stubborn and rebelled, choosing a leader to take them back to slavery. Yet you are a God who readily forgives, gracious and merciful, slow to get angry, and full of steadfast love. You stayed with them.
They even cast a calf for themselves and said, 'This is your god who brought you out of Egypt.' They spoke outrageously against you.
Still, in your great mercy, you stayed with them in the wilderness. The pillar of cloud kept leading them during the day, and the pillar of fire kept lighting their way at night.
You gave them your good Spirit to teach them. You kept giving them manna to eat and water to drink.
For forty years you sustained them in the wilderness. They lacked nothing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet didn't swell.
You gave them kingdoms and peoples, allotting them their portions. They took possession of the land of Sihon, king of Heshbon, and the land of Og, king of Bashan.
You made their children as numerous as the stars in the sky and brought them into the land you had told their ancestors to possess.
Their children entered and took the land. You subdued the Canaanites who lived there and handed their kings and people over to them to deal with as they pleased.

They captured fortified cities and took fertile land, houses full of good things, cisterns already dug, vineyards, olive groves, and many fruit trees. They ate until they were full, grew fat, and enjoyed your great goodness.
Even so, they disobeyed and rebelled against you. They turned their backs on your law and killed your prophets who warned them to come back to you. They did outrageous things against you.
So you handed them over to enemies who oppressed them. When they cried out in distress, you heard from heaven. In your great mercy you gave them rescuers who saved them from their enemies.

Once they had peace, they did evil again in your sight. You left them in their enemies' hands and let those enemies rule over them. Yet when they turned back and cried out to you, you heard from heaven and rescued them time after time in your mercy.

You warned them to return to your law. They acted arrogantly and ignored your commands, sinning against your rulings even though anyone who keeps them will live by them. They turned their backs, grew stubborn, and refused to listen.
You put up with them for years and warned them by your Spirit through your prophets. They refused to listen, so you handed them over to the peoples of other lands.
Yet in your great mercy you didn't destroy them completely or abandon them. You are a gracious and merciful God.

So now, our God, great, mighty, and awesome, you keep your covenant and show steadfast love. Please take seriously all the suffering that has come on us, our kings, officials, priests, prophets, ancestors, and all your people, from the days of the kings of Assyria until today.
You've acted justly in everything that's happened to us. You've been faithful, and we've done wrong.
Our kings, officials, priests, and ancestors failed to keep your law or listen to the commands and warnings you gave them.
Even in their own kingdom, with all the good things you gave them and the wide, fertile land you set before them, they refused to serve you or turn from their wicked deeds.
And here we are today, servants in the very land you gave our ancestors so they could eat its fruit and enjoy its good things.
Its abundant harvest goes to the kings you've set over us because of our sins. They have power over our bodies and livestock and do as they please. We're in great distress.
In light of all this, we're making a binding agreement and putting it in writing. Our leaders, Levites, and priests are setting their seals on it."
The people who sealed the agreement were Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah,
Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah,
Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah,
Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch,
Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah,
Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch,
Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin,
Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah. These were the priests.
The Levites were Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui from Henadad's family, and Kadmiel,
along with their fellow Levites Shebaniah, Hodiah, Kelita, Pelaiah, and Hanan,
Mica, Rehob, Hashabiah,
Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah,
Hodiah, Bani, and Beninu.
The leaders of the people were Parosh, Pahathmoab, Elam, Zattu, and Bani,
Bunni, Azgad, Bebai,
Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin,
Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur,
Hodiah, Hashum, Bezai,
Hariph, Anathoth, Nobai,
Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir,
Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua,
Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah,
Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub,
Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek,
Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah,
Ahiah, Hanan, Anan,
Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

The rest of the people joined them: priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and everyone who had separated themselves from the peoples of the land to follow God's law, together with their wives, sons, and daughters who were old enough to understand.

They joined their fellow Israelites, the nobles, in an oath backed by a curse. They pledged to live by God's law given through his servant Moses and carefully obey all the commands, rulings, and statutes of the LORD our Lord.
We pledged neither to give our daughters in marriage to the peoples of the land nor to take their daughters as wives for our sons.
If the peoples of the land brought goods or grain to sell on a Sabbath or a holy day, we would buy nothing from them. In the seventh year we would let the land rest and cancel all debts.
We agreed that each of us would give a third of a shekel each year for the service of our God's house.

It would pay for the sacred bread, the regular grain and burnt offerings, the offerings for Sabbaths, new moons, and appointed festivals, the sacred gifts, the sin offerings to make atonement for Israel, and all the work of our God's house.
We priests, Levites, and people drew lots by family to decide when we would bring wood to our God's house each year to burn on the altar of the LORD our God, as the law says.
We also agreed to bring the first produce from our fields and from every kind of fruit tree to the LORD's house each year.
As written in the law, we would bring our firstborn sons and firstborn animals, including the firstborn of our herds and flocks, to the priests serving in the house of our God.

We agreed to bring the priests the first of our dough, our wave offerings, the fruit of every kind of tree, new wine, and oil, to be kept in the storerooms of our God's house. We would give the Levites a tenth of our produce because they collect the tithes in all our farming towns.
A priest descended from Aaron must be with the Levites when they collect the tithes. The Levites must bring a tenth of those tithes to the storerooms in the treasury of our God's house.

The Israelites and Levites must bring their offerings of grain, new wine, and oil to the storerooms where the sanctuary vessels are kept and where the serving priests, gatekeepers, and singers are. We will take care of the house of our God.
The leaders of the people lived in Jerusalem. The rest drew lots so that one person in ten would live in Jerusalem, the holy city, and the other nine would stay in the other towns.
The people blessed everyone who volunteered to live in Jerusalem.

These are the leaders of the province who lived in Jerusalem. In the other towns of Judah, the Israelites, priests, Levites, temple servants, and descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property.
Some people from Judah and Benjamin lived in Jerusalem. From Judah came Athaiah son of Uzziah, whose ancestors were Zechariah, Amariah, Shephatiah, and Mahalalel, from the line of Perez.
There was also Maaseiah son of Baruch, whose ancestors were Colhozeh, Hazaiah, Adaiah, Joiarib, Zechariah, and the Shilonite.
There were four hundred sixty-eight capable men from the line of Perez living in Jerusalem.
From Benjamin came Sallu son of Meshullam, whose ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah.
Gabbai and Sallai came after him. The group numbered nine hundred twenty-eight.
Joel son of Zichri supervised them, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in charge of the city.
The priests included Jedaiah son of Joiarib, Jachin,
and Seraiah son of Hilkiah, whose ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been in charge of God's house.

They and their fellow priests who worked at God's house numbered eight hundred twenty-two. There was also Adaiah son of Jeroham, whose ancestors were Pelaliah, Amzi, Zechariah, Pashhur, and Malchijah.
Adaiah's fellow family heads numbered two hundred forty-two. There was also Amashsai son of Azarel, whose ancestors were Ahzai, Meshillemoth, and Immer.
He and his fellow men of courage numbered a hundred twenty-eight, and Zabdiel son of Haggedolim supervised them.
The Levites included Shemaiah son of Hasshub, whose ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni,
along with Shabbethai and Jozabad, Levite leaders who supervised work outside God's house.

There was also Mattaniah son of Mica, descended from Zabdi and Asaph, who led the prayer of thanksgiving. Bakbukiah was second among his fellow Levites. Abda was the son of Shammua, descended from Galal and Jeduthun.
There were two hundred eighty-four Levites in the holy city.
The gatekeepers Akkub, Talmon, and their fellow guards numbered a hundred seventy-two. They kept watch at the gates.
The other Israelites, priests, and Levites lived in the towns of Judah, each on their own inherited land.
The temple servants lived on Ophel, with Ziha and Gishpa in charge of them.
Uzzi son of Bani supervised the Levites in Jerusalem. His ancestors were Hashabiah, Mattaniah, and Mica, from Asaph's family of singers responsible for the service of God's house.
The king had issued instructions about them, with a fixed provision for what the singers needed each day.
Pethahiah son of Meshezabel, a descendant of Judah's son Zerah, represented the people in all matters before the king.
As for the villages and their fields, some of Judah's people settled in Kiriath Arba and its surrounding towns, in Dibon and its towns, and in Jekabzeel and its villages.
Others settled in Jeshua, Moladah, and Beth Pelet,
in Hazar Shual and in Beersheba and its towns,
in Ziklag and in Meconah and its towns,
in En Rimmon, Zorah, and Jarmuth,
in Zanoah and Adullam with their villages, in Lachish and its fields, and in Azekah and its towns. They settled from Beersheba to the Valley of Hinnom.
The people of Benjamin settled from Geba onward, in Michmash, Aija, and Bethel and its towns,
and in Anathoth, Nob, and Ananiah,
Hazor, Ramah, and Gittaim,
Hadid, Zeboim, and Neballat,
as well as Lod and Ono, the Valley of the Craftsmen.
Some divisions of Levites from Judah settled in Benjamin's territory.
These are the priests and Levites who came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
Amariah, Malluch, Hattush,
Shecaniah, Rehum, Meremoth,
Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah,
Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah,
Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah,
and Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. They were the leaders of the priests and their fellow priests in Jeshua's time.
The Levites included Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. Mattaniah and his brothers led the songs of thanksgiving.
Their fellow Levites Bakbukiah and Unno stood next to them in their assigned places.
Jeshua was the father of Joiakim, Joiakim of Eliashib, and Eliashib of Joiada.
Joiada was the father of Jonathan, and Jonathan was the father of Jaddua.
In Joiakim's time, these priests headed their families: Meraiah led Seraiah's family, and Hananiah led Jeremiah's.
Meshullam led Ezra's family, and Jehohanan led Amariah's.
Jonathan led Malluchi's family, and Joseph led Shebaniah's.
Adna led Harim's family, and Helkai led Meraioth's.
Zechariah led Iddo's family, and Meshullam led Ginnethon's.
Zichri led Abijah's family. Miniamin's family was listed, and Piltai led Moadiah's.
Shammua led Bilgah's family, and Jehonathan led Shemaiah's.
Mattenai led Joiarib's family, and Uzzi led Jedaiah's.
Kallai led Sallai's family, and Eber led Amok's.
Hashabiah led Hilkiah's family, and Nethanel led Jedaiah's.
The heads of the Levite families were recorded in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and the priests were recorded during the reign of Darius the Persian.
The heads of the Levite families were listed in the Book of the Chronicles through the time of Johanan son of Eliashib.
Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel led the Levites. They and their fellow Levites stood group by group to give praise and thanks as David, the man of God, had commanded.
Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were gatekeepers who guarded the storerooms at the gates.
These men served in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and in the days of Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest and scribe.

At the dedication of Jerusalem's wall, the people called the Levites from wherever they lived to come to Jerusalem and celebrate the dedication with joy, with thanksgiving, singing, cymbals, stringed instruments, and harps.
The singers gathered from the plain around Jerusalem and from the villages of the Netophathites.
They also came from Beth Gilgal and the fields of Geba and Azmaveth, because they'd built villages for themselves around Jerusalem.
The priests and Levites purified themselves, then purified the people, the gates, and the wall.
I brought Judah's leaders up on the wall and appointed two large groups to give thanks and walk in procession. One group went to the right along the wall toward the Dung Gate.
Hoshaiah followed them with half of Judah's officials,
along with Azariah, Ezra, and Meshullam,
Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, and Jeremiah.
Some descendants of priests came with trumpets, including Zechariah son of Jonathan. His line went back through Shemaiah, Mattaniah, Micaiah, and Zaccur to Asaph.
His relatives Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani carried the musical instruments of David, the man of God. Ezra the scribe led them.
At the Spring Gate they went straight up the steps of the City of David, where the wall climbs above David's house, and continued east to the Water Gate.
The other group giving thanks went the opposite way to meet them. I followed with half the people along the wall, past the Tower of the Furnaces and on to the Broad Wall.
We went past the Ephraim Gate, the Old Gate, the Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, and the Tower of Hammeah, as far as the Sheep Gate. We stopped at the Guard Gate.
Both groups giving thanks then took their places in God's house. I was there with half the officials,
along with the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah with trumpets,
and Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang loudly under the direction of Jezrahiah.
They offered many sacrifices that day and celebrated because God had given them great joy. The women and children celebrated too. Jerusalem's joy could be heard far away.

That day men were appointed over the storerooms for treasures, wave offerings, first produce, and tithes. They were to collect from the fields around the towns the portions the law assigned to the priests and Levites, because the people of Judah were glad for the priests and Levites who served.
The priests and Levites carried out the service of their God and the duties of purification. The singers and gatekeepers did their work too, as David and his son Solomon had commanded.
Long ago in the days of David and Asaph there was a leader of the singers, and there were songs of praise and thanksgiving to God.

In the days of Zerubbabel and Nehemiah, all Israel supplied what the singers and gatekeepers needed each day. They set aside the Levites' share, and the Levites set aside the share for Aaron's descendants.
That day the Book of Moses was read aloud to the people. They found it written there that Ammonites and Moabites were never to enter God's assembly,
because they hadn't met the Israelites with bread and water, and instead hired Balaam to curse them. Our God turned the curse into a blessing.
When the people heard the law, they separated everyone of foreign descent from Israel.
Before this, Eliashib the priest, who was in charge of the storerooms in our God's house, had become an ally of Tobiah.

He had made a large room available to Tobiah where they used to store the grain offerings, incense, vessels, and tithes of grain, new wine, and oil required for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, along with the offerings for the priests.
I was away from Jerusalem while this happened. In the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes, king of Babylon, I had gone back to the king. After a while I asked his permission to leave,
and when I returned to Jerusalem, I learned what a wrong Eliashib had done in giving Tobiah a room in the courtyards of God's house.
I was deeply upset, so I threw all Tobiah's belongings out of the room.
I ordered the rooms purified, then brought back the vessels of God's house, the grain offerings, and the incense.
I also found out that the Levites hadn't been given their shares. The Levites and singers who served had gone back to their fields.
I confronted the officials and asked, "Why has God's house been neglected?" Then I called the Levites and singers together and put them back at their posts.
All Judah brought the tithes of grain, new wine, and oil into the storerooms.

I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah the Levite in charge of the storerooms, with Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, as their assistant. They were considered trustworthy, and their job was to distribute the shares to their fellow workers.
My God, remember me for this. Don't erase the good I've done for your house and its worship.

In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath, gathering bundles of grain, and loading donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and goods of every kind. They were bringing them into Jerusalem on the Sabbath. I warned them that day as they sold their food.
People from Tyre who lived there were also bringing in fish and all kinds of goods and selling them to the people of Judah in Jerusalem on the Sabbath.
I confronted Judah's nobles and said, "Why are you doing this evil thing and treating the Sabbath like any other day?
Didn't your ancestors do the same thing, and didn't our God bring all this disaster on us and this city? Now you're bringing more anger on Israel by profaning the Sabbath."

As darkness fell at Jerusalem's gates before the Sabbath, I ordered the doors shut and told them to keep them closed until the Sabbath was over. I stationed some of my men at the gates so no loads would be brought in on the Sabbath.
Once or twice the merchants and sellers of all kinds of goods spent the night outside Jerusalem.
I warned them, "Why are you camping by the wall? If you do it again, I'll have you seized." From then on they stopped coming on the Sabbath.
I told the Levites to purify themselves and come guard the gates to keep the Sabbath holy. My God, remember me for this too, and spare me in your great faithful love.
In those days I also saw Jews who had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
Half their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and others spoke the languages of the other peoples. They didn't know how to speak the language of Judah.

I confronted them, cursed them, struck some of them, and pulled out their hair. I made them swear by God, "You must never give your daughters to their sons or take their daughters as wives for your sons or for yourselves.
Isn't this how King Solomon of Israel sinned? Among many nations there was no king like him. His God loved him and made him king over all Israel. Yet foreign women led even him into sin.
Are we supposed to hear that you've done this great wrong and been unfaithful to our God by marrying foreign women?"
One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, had married a daughter of Sanballat the Horonite, so I drove him away.
My God, remember them for defiling the priesthood and the covenant of the priests and Levites.
So I cleansed them of everything foreign and assigned the priests and Levites their duties, each to his own work.
I also arranged for the wood offerings at the appointed times and for the first produce. My God, remember me for good.
